verdict: The publisher-issued 2015 booklet supports a labeled, source-cited clarification that two Town Hall occupants may be sent in separate action turns in the same Action Phase before the player passes. Keeping the unused occupant until its later turn is a necessary implication of the expressly referenced separate-actions permission. The booklet does not expressly settle retention across rounds after only one of two occupants was sent.

scope.question: Effect of using one of two Town Hall occupants on the other occupant, with no expansion procedures adopted.
sources_read: base-clarification-invasion-extraction.txt: relevant p3 text and publication credit
scope.excluded_material: No summaries, question banks, keys, reader outputs, grades, coverage reviews, web sources, or prior game knowledge used.

supported_conclusions.claim: A Town Hall with two occupants may send just one of them in an action; a single occupant is sufficient to activate Town Hall.
The 2015 publisher text explicitly invokes Town Hall as the precedent for using any or all placed tiles in the same action or in separate actions.
supported_conclusions.support_level: Explicit cross-reference; the sentence grammatically describes the Carpenter but expressly identifies Town Hall as sharing this feature.

supported_conclusions.claim: A labeled FAQ clarification may say that two Town Hall Followers can be sent one per action turn within the same Action Phase, before the player passes.
supported_conclusions.support_level: Source-supported application of the explicit Town Hall analogy, combined with base action-turn and passing rules. This is not the title or wording of an official FAQ.

supported_conclusions.claim: After sending the first, the second Follower must be permitted to remain in Town Hall until the later action turn if the player chooses the expressly permitted separate-actions option.
supported_conclusions.support_level: Necessary implication, not a verbatim retention instruction. Returning that second tile to the bag immediately would prevent the described separate use of the already placed tiles.

supported_conclusions.claim: A wholly unused activated action may remain activated into a later round.
supported_conclusions.support_level: Explicit general base rule; its application to a partially used Town Hall is a separate interpretive step.

unsupported_or_not_expressly_established.claim: The 2015 booklet explicitly says that a Town Hall Follower left after a partial use remains through the end of the round and into subsequent rounds.
unsupported_or_not_expressly_established.assessment: Not expressly established. The p3 analogy says separate actions, without specifying separate rounds. Combining it with base p15 retention of unused activated actions makes cross-round retention a plausible inference, but p15 speaks of actions not used this round and does not expressly classify a partially used Town Hall.

unsupported_or_not_expressly_established.claim: A player may use Town Hall again after passing in the same round.
unsupported_or_not_expressly_established.assessment: Contradicted by base p15. Separate action turns must occur before the player passes.

unsupported_or_not_expressly_established.claim: Carpenter movement, repeated construction, return-to-bag treatment of used Carpenter tiles, or any other scenario procedure applies to Town Hall.
unsupported_or_not_expressly_established.assessment: Unsupported and unnecessary. Only the expressly stated common any/all and same/separate-actions feature is used. Base Town Hall sends its used tiles to Beneficial Deeds, where they remain.

unsupported_or_not_expressly_established.claim: This document is a formal erratum that explicitly changes or supersedes the 2014 Town Hall rule.
unsupported_or_not_expressly_established.assessment: Unsupported. The relevant sentence presents Town Hall as an existing precedent, rather than announcing a change.

edition_compatibility.publisher_authorship_evidence: The inspected 2015 PDF bears the dlp games logo, copyright, website, and publisher email on printed p24. The local provenance record identifies a third-party host; it is supporting provenance rather than independent proof of every edition detail.
edition_compatibility.assessment: Compatible as a later publisher-authored clarification of the specific Town Hall behavior in the supplied 2014 base text. The base allows one or both occupants to be sent and does not require both spaces for activation; the 2015 analogy explains how separate use works. Nothing in the cited passage announces an altered Town Hall rule.
edition_compatibility.limit: Compatibility is an interpretation of the supplied wording, not proof that every rule or every later base edition is unchanged. The generic p15 cleanup text alone is broad enough to produce the original ambiguity; the specific Town Hall cross-reference resolves its immediate-clearance reading for separate action turns.

proposed_labeled_faq.label: Publisher clarification: Town Hall separate action turns (2015 booklet, p3)
proposed_labeled_faq.text: If two Followers occupy your Town Hall, you may send both in one Town Hall action or send one now and leave the other for a later action turn in the same Action Phase. Take that later action before you pass. This follows the publisher’s explicit Town Hall comparison in the 2015 booklet; it does not claim an explicit ruling about carrying a partially used Town Hall into another round.
proposed_labeled_faq.retention_wording_status: Leave the other is a necessary implication of separate use, not a direct quotation.

essential_gap.reason: The explicit publisher Town Hall analogy supports separate use of the already placed occupants. Its necessary retention implication resolves whether generic cleanup immediately forces the untransferred occupant into the bag before the second same-round action.
essential_gap.cross_round_status: A further inference, not a direct statement in the inspected clarification. Do not present it as explicitly established by p3.
essential_gap.if_cross_round_answer_is_required: An additional explicit publisher or designer statement addressing the untransferred tile at round end after partial Town Hall use would resolve the remaining narrow evidentiary question. No judgment is made about unrelated essential gaps or unseen QA material.
